problem_name: Inability to Determine Eligibility for Government Legal Aid (NLASO Means Test Opacity)
stakeholders: Indigent Citizens; Marginalized Litigants; NLASO Staff; District Legal Aid Officers
root_cause: Income thresholds (BDT 100,000/yr for individuals, BDT 150,000/yr for women/children under NLASO gazette) are obscure, requiring complex manual documentation like Union Parishad income certificates that are prone to gatekeeping.
one_line_solution: Multilingual conversational AI means-test validator connected via WhatsApp/SMS that assesses legal aid eligibility in 90 seconds.
existing_solutions: Physical visits to District Legal Aid Offices; 16430 National Legal Aid Helpline; sporadic NGO informational brochures.
existing_gaps: No real-time self-assessment tool; algorithmic means testing absent; lack of integration with national social safety net (NID/SSNP) databases.

problem_name: Exploitation by Courtroom Middlemen (Dalaal Network Extortion)
stakeholders: First-Time Litigants; Rural Citizens; Court Security; Bar Council
root_cause: Asymmetry of court navigation knowledge; intimidating physical architecture; lack of official front-desk navigation or digital wayfinding.
one_line_solution: Verified digital legal service marketplace with transparent fixed-fee or legal-aid matching and broker-alert GPS-fenced reporting.
existing_solutions: Occasional anti-broker police drives; static notice boards; bar association identity cards.
existing_gaps: Broker networks bypass physical checks; no verified digital directory of pro-bono advocates or authorized fees; no direct citizen booking channel.
technology_tags: Verified Directory; Marketplace Engine; Geo-Fencing; Whistleblower Tech; Reputation Scoring

problem_name: Prohibitive Out-of-Pocket Travel and Daily Wage Loss for Routine Adjournments ('Taarikhe Taarikh')
stakeholders: Daily Wage Laborers; Rural Farmers; Garment Workers; District Judges
root_cause: Court procedural requirement of physical appearance for perfunctory date extensions without actual hearings taking place.
one_line_solution: Predictive hearing adjournment SMS notification and asynchronous virtual procedural appearance module.
existing_solutions: Lawyer appearances without client; occasional virtual court pilots; cause list publication on website.
existing_gaps: Cause lists updated late at night; no automated SMS notifications; no virtual appearance option for non-substantive procedural dates.

problem_name: Incomprehensible Legal Jargon and Cognitive Alienation from English Court Orders
stakeholders: Citizens; High Court Litigants; Paralegals; Community Legal Workers
root_cause: Colonial legal syntax and Supreme Court/High Court judgments delivered primarily in complex English or formal Sadhu-Bhasha legalese.
one_line_solution: Domain-tuned legal LLM that ingests High Court judgment PDFs and outputs 3-bullet plain-language Bangla audio summaries.
existing_solutions: Lawyers verbally summarizing orders; sporadic manual translations by legal portals; manual court summaries.
existing_gaps: No automated plain-language Bangla simplifier; legal terms translated inaccurately by standard Google Translate; no audio explanation for illiterate citizens.

problem_name: Total Darkness on Bail Status of Incarcerated Family Members
stakeholders: Families of Detainees; Under-Trial Prisoners (UTPs); Jail Authorities; Legal Aid Lawyers
root_cause: Disconnected paper records between District Sessions Courts, Chief Judicial Magistrate Courts, and Central/District Jails.
one_line_solution: Cryptographically signed digital bail transfer network (FastBail-BD) linking courts to prison gates with automated SMS alerts to families.
existing_solutions: Physical prison gate visits (Mulaqat); informal bribes to peons or wardens; private lawyer telephone calls.
existing_gaps: No publicly searchable prison bail tracking portal; delay of 7-15 days in transmitting paper bail release orders (release perwana).

problem_name: Fear of Retaliation and Lack of Anonymous Reporting for Local Land Grabbing

existing_solutions: National emergency 999; Anti-Corruption Commission hotline 106; physical writ petitions.

root_cause: Cumbersome paper voucher auditing processes; manual submission of cause list proof; bureaucratic multi-tier government accounting clearance.

existing_solutions: Projects by Supreme Court publishing select decisions; private database subscriptions.
existing_gaps: Coverage incomplete; much content only in English; no search by Bangla.
technology_tags: AI; NLP; DataScience; Cloud

problem_name: Insufficient Forensic and Expert Support
root_cause: Sparse forensic labs; delayed reports; judges hearing technical cases without expertise; evidence often mishandled.
one_line_solution: Implement a digital evidence submission and tracking system linked to labs and courts, with mobile collection kits.
existing_solutions: NFIU (national forensic institute) expansion; some DNA testing units.
existing_gaps: Geographic access limited; no digital evidence chain; backlogs in labs.
technology_tags: Blockchain; ComputerVision; Mobile; Cloud

problem_name: Gender and Bias in Judgments
root_cause: Implicit bias; lack of gender-sensitivity training; cultural norms influence decisions; few female judges (women’s issues often heard by men).
one_line_solution: Develop an AI-assisted review tool to flag non-compliance with gender-sensitive legal standards in draft judgments.
existing_solutions: Workshops on gender justice for judges; special rules for domestic violence cases.
existing_gaps: Training not institutionalized; no AI flagging of biased language; no diversity quotas.
technology_tags: AI; NLP; Cloud

problem_name: Pressure and Security Concerns for Judges
stakeholders: Judges; Crime Victims; Accused; Civil Society
root_cause: High-profile cases attract threats; lack of protection for judges; no secure communication channels; intimidation by powerful actors.
one_line_solution: Introduce secure telepresence for sensitive cases and confidential reporting apps for judges.
existing_solutions: Some secure court buildings; police protection for high-risk judges.
existing_gaps: No anonymized hearing or remote witness tools; no secure reporting for threats.
technology_tags: Cybersecurity; VideoConferencing; Blockchain

problem_name: Manual Case Recording and Scheduling
root_cause: Case details logged in ledgers or local Excel; no automated scheduling; repeated adjournments due to conflicts.
one_line_solution: Implement a digital case management and automated scheduling system with SMS/email notifications.
existing_solutions: Trial e-Court systems in high courts; paper calendars.
existing_gaps: Outdated at district courts; no mobile updates to parties; high adjournment rates.
technology_tags: SoftwareEngineering; Mobile; DataScience

problem_name: Infrastructure Limitations (Hardware/Connectivity)
stakeholders: Court Staff; Judges; Litigants; Govt IT
root_cause: Poor electricity reliability; limited computers/printers; slow internet; physical buildings lack modernization.
one_line_solution: Roll out cloud-based thin-client solutions with solar backup in every court.
existing_solutions: A2I (a2i) projects to equip some courts; solar power in pilot courts.
existing_gaps: Many lower courts still offline; backups rare; hardware outdated.
technology_tags: Cloud; ICT Infrastructure; Mobile

problem_name: Lack of Unified Justice Information System
root_cause: Different agencies maintain separate databases; no common ID or case identifier; no centralized data sharing.
one_line_solution: Build an interoperable justice information exchange platform linking police, courts, prisons, and legal aid with unique case IDs.
existing_solutions: Justice Sector Data Center (pilot); e-Registry for Supreme Court.
existing_gaps: Integrated platform not implemented; manual data exchange; duplication of records.
technology_tags: Interoperability; Cloud; DataScience

problem_name: Insufficient Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) Integration
stakeholders: Court Administrators; Judges; Litigants; Legal Aid Departments
root_cause: Culture favors litigation; ADR (mediation, arbitration) is decentralized; no tech integration for ADR processes.
one_line_solution: Develop an online ADR management portal that tracks mediation cases and links to court outcomes.
existing_solutions: District Legal Aid Committees offer mediation; family courts have conciliation cells.
existing_gaps: ADR uptake still low; no online ADR case management; no enforcement of mediated settlements digitally.
technology_tags: SoftwareEngineering; Mobile; Blockchain

problem_name: Poor Public Engagement and Feedback Mechanisms
root_cause: Courts operate opaquely; no systematic public surveys or grievance portals; limited transparency.
one_line_solution: Create a public-facing dashboard with court performance metrics and an e-grievance submission system.
existing_solutions: Suggestion boxes in some courts; occasional public hearings.
existing_gaps: No digital portal for complaints/feedback; no published service standards.
technology_tags: DataScience; Cloud; Mobile

problem_name: Fragmented Justice Sector Policies
stakeholders: Executive Branch; Legislature; Judiciary; Ministry of Law; Citizens
root_cause: Multiple agencies (home, law, local govt) involved with little coordination; policies overlap or leave gaps; slow policy response.
one_line_solution: Establish an e-justice task force to harmonize policies and standards across ministries.
existing_solutions: Inter-ministerial committees (e.g., CCCs in prisons).
existing_gaps: Formal coordination lacking for digital justice; disconnected e-gov initiatives.
technology_tags: eGovernment; DataScience

problem_name: Insufficient Budget Allocation for Justice
stakeholders: Parliament; Ministry of Finance; Law Ministry; Courts; Public
root_cause: Competing priorities (health, education); justice often underfunded; political focus elsewhere; lack cost-benefit analysis.
one_line_solution: Introduce a transparent e-budgeting platform showing justice sector needs and impact indicators to drive funding.
existing_solutions: Occasional donor-funded projects; increasing law ministry share slightly.
existing_gaps: Reliance on aid; many planned reforms unfunded; no performance-based budgeting.

problem_name: Slow Digital Government Services
stakeholders: Government IT Agencies; Citizens; Justice Sector Agencies
root_cause: Legacy systems; bureaucratic procurement; lack agile development; siloed apps; low digital literacy among officials.
one_line_solution: Launch a unified justice portal (single sign-on) that federates data from courts, police, prisons, using open APIs.
existing_solutions: “Digital Bangladesh” programs; some e-government services (e-Nothi for government docs).
existing_gaps: E-services often not integrated with justice; citizen-centric design lacking; heavy dependency on foreign platforms.

problem_name: Absence of Standards for Legal Tech and AI
stakeholders: Ministry of ICT; Law Ministry; Bar; Civil Society
root_cause: Regulatory gap for new technologies (AI, e-signed documents, digital evidence); no guidelines or legislation on AI in courts.
one_line_solution: Draft a national “E-Justice Act” setting standards for digital evidence, e-filing, and AI use in courts.
existing_solutions: General ICT policy; nascent Digital Security Act (2018).
existing_gaps: No law on electronic evidence specifics; no AI ethics framework for judiciary.

problem_name: Low Public Trust in Government Justice Initiatives
root_cause: Perceived corruption; lack of transparency in decision-making; delayed reforms; poor communication; neglect of vulnerable.
one_line_solution: Introduce open-data portals and participatory policymaking apps for citizens to track justice projects and provide input.
existing_solutions: Public messaging campaigns (National Legal Aid Day).
existing_gaps: Skepticism persists; initiatives not always visible in rural areas; lack feedback loops.

problem_name: Weak Legislative Drafting Capacity
stakeholders: Ministry of Law; Parliamentary Affairs; Legislators; Legal Drafters
root_cause: Limited specialized personnel; no modern drafting tools; drafts often copy-paste outdated text; minimal public consultation.
one_line_solution: Develop an AI-assisted legislative drafting tool that suggests clauses from global best practice and checks consistency.
existing_solutions: Training by law commissions; consulting firms.
existing_gaps: No internal legal tech; no version-control or collaboration tools; no automated plain-language conversion.

problem_name: Siloed Justice Sector Coordination
root_cause: Historical separation of responsibilities; poor information flow; lack of joint mandates.
one_line_solution: Create an interagency digital dashboard for real-time case monitoring and task tracking across ministries.
existing_solutions: MoUs between MLJPA and other bodies (e.g., with NLASO).
existing_gaps: Implementation of MoUs slow; no central digital coordination platform.

problem_name: Limited Engagement with Private Sector/Startups
root_cause: Procurement rules not startup-friendly; perception that justice tech is niche; no incubator for legal innovation.
one_line_solution: Establish a government-backed legal tech innovation lab and cloud sandbox for startups to pilot solutions.

existing_gaps: No legal incubator or challenge fund; brain-drain of tech talent.

problem_name: Inadequate Data on Justice Sector Performance
